en: Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub and Yunus, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: I went out intending to support this man, but Abu Bakrah met me and asked, "Where are you heading, O Ahnaf?" I said, "I intend to support the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him—meaning 'Ali." He said to me, "O Ahnaf, turn back, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: 'When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, both the killer and the killed are in the Fire.'" He said: I said—or it was said—"O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the one who was killed?" He said: "He also intended to kill his companion."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, both from 'Uthman ash-Shahham with this chain of narration. The hadith of Ibn Abi 'Adi is similar to the hadith of Hammad to its end, while the hadith of Waki' ended at his words: "if he is able to escape," and he did not mention what came after it.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari, Fudayl ibn Husayn, narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: 'Uthman ash-Shahham narrated to us, saying: Farqad as-Sabakhi and I set out to Muslim ibn Abi Bakrah while he was on his land. We entered upon him and said, "Have you heard your father narrate any hadith concerning tribulations?" He said: Yes, I heard Abu Bakrah narrate that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, there will be tribulations. Beware, then there will be a tribulation in which the one sitting will be better than the one walking, and the one walking in it will be better than the one striving toward it. Beware, so when it descends or occurs, whoever has camels should join his camels, whoever has sheep should join his sheep, and whoever has land should join his land." A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if someone has neither camels, nor sheep, nor land?" He said: "He should take hold of his sword and strike its edge with a stone, then escape if he is able to escape. O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed?" A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I am forced until I am taken to one of the two ranks or one of the two factions, and a man strikes me with his sword, or an arrow comes and kills me?" He said: "He will bear his own sin and your sin, and he will be among the companions of the Fire."

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abu Dawud at-Tayalisi reported to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There will be a tribulation in which the one sleeping will be better than the one awake, the one awake in it will be better than the one standing, and the one standing in it will be better than the one striving. So whoever finds a refuge or a shelter should take refuge."

'Amr an-Naqid, al-Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—'Abd said: reported to me, and the other two said: Ya'qub narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman narrated to me, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Muti' ibn al-Aswad, from Nawfal ibn Mu'awiyah, similar to this hadith of Abu Hurayrah, except that Abu Bakr added: "Among the prayers is a prayer such that whoever misses it, it is as though he has been deprived of his family and his wealth."

'Amr an-Naqid, al-Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: reported to me, and the other two said: Ya'qub—namely Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There will be tribulations in which the one sitting will be better than the one standing, and the one standing in it will be better than the one walking, and the one walking in it will be better than the one striving. Whoever exposes himself to them, they will overcome him; and whoever finds a refuge in them, let him take shelter in it."
'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us: Ma'mar reported to us, from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, similar to it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr an-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's; Ishaq said: reported to us, while the others said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Usamah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, looked down from one of the fortresses of Madinah, then said: "Do you see what I see? Indeed, I see the places where tribulations fall amidst your houses like the falling of raindrops."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Huddani narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr, that 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, moved restlessly in his sleep, so we said, "O Messenger of Allah, you did something in your sleep that you used not to do." He said: "How astonishing! Indeed, some people of my nation will head toward the House seeking a man of Quraysh who has taken refuge in the House, until when they are in the desert plain, the earth will swallow them up." We said, "O Messenger of Allah, the road may gather different people." He said: "Yes, among them are those who come with insight, those who are coerced, and the wayfarer; they will perish in one destruction, but will be resurrected in diverse states; Allah will resurrect them according to their intentions."

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Al-Walid ibn Salih narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us: Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik al-'Amiri, from Yusuf ibn Mahak: 'Abdullah ibn Safwan reported to me, from the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "A people with no protection, no great numbers, and no equipment will take refuge in this House—meaning the Ka'bah. An army will be sent against them until, when they reach an open desert of the earth, the earth will swallow them up." Yusuf said: At that time, the people of the Levant were marching toward Makkah, so 'Abdullah ibn Safwan said, "By Allah, it is not this army." Zayd said: And 'Abd al-Malik al-'Amiri narrated to me, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit, from al-Harith ibn Abi Rabi'ah, from the Mother of the Believers, similar to the hadith of Yusuf ibn Mahak, except that he did not mention the army that 'Abdullah ibn Safwan mentioned.

'Amr an-Naqid and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is 'Amr's—they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Umayyah ibn Safwan, who heard his grandfather 'Abdullah ibn Safwan say: Hafsah reported to me that she heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "An army will certainly head toward this House to attack it until, when they are in an open desert of the earth, the middle of them will be swallowed by the earth, and their first will call out to their last, then they will all be swallowed up, so that none will remain except a fugitive who will report about them." A man said, "I bear witness concerning you that you did not lie about Hafsah, and I bear witness concerning Hafsah that she did not lie about the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him."

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated it to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay' narrated to us with this chain of narration, and in his hadith he said: I met Abu Ja'far and said, "She only said: 'in an open desert of the earth.'" Abu Ja'far said, "By no means, by Allah! Indeed, it is the desert of Madinah."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Qutaybah's; Ishaq said: reported to us, while the other two said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', from 'Ubaydullah ibn al-Qibtiyyah, who said: Al-Harith ibn Abi Rabi'ah and 'Abdullah ibn Safwan, while I was with them, entered upon Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers, and asked her about the army that would be swallowed by the earth, and that was during the days of Ibn az-Zubayr. She said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "A seeker of refuge will seek refuge in the House, so a force will be sent against him. When they are in an open desert of the earth, they will be swallowed up." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about the one who was unwilling?" He said: "He will be swallowed along with them, but he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to his intention." Abu Ja'far said: "It is the desert of Madinah."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Tawus narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Today a hole like this has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog." And Wuhayb clasped ninety with his hand.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me; (and a different chain) 'Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, both from Ibn Shihab, similar to the hadith of Yunus from az-Zuhri with his chain of narration.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Yunus reported to me, from Ibn Shihab: 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr reported to me that Zaynab bint Abi Salamah reported to him that Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan reported to her that Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: One day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out agitated, his face flushed red, saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today, a hole like this has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog." And he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. She said: I asked, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness becomes widespread."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration. And they added to the chain from Sufyan, saying: from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Habibah, from Umm Habibah, from Zaynab bint Jahsh.

'Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Habibah, from Zaynab bint Jahsh, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, woke from his sleep saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today, a hole like this has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog." And Sufyan clasped ten with his hand. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness becomes widespread."

Harmalah ibn Yahya at-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Yunus reported to me, from Ibn Shihab: Hamzah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar reported to me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "When Allah wills punishment for a people, the punishment afflicts whoever is among them, then they are resurrected according to their deeds."

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, the like of it; and he said: "from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him," and did not say: "I heard."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah both narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Every servant will be resurrected upon what he died upon."

Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to me: Abu an-Nu'man 'Arim narrated to us: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us: Wasil narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say three days before his death: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus and Abu Mu'awiyah reported to us, all of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yahya ibn Zakariyya reported to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say three days before his passing: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah."

'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to me: Yahya—namely al-Qattan—narrated to me, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Whoever is called to a detailed reckoning will perish." Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Abu Yunus.

'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-'Abdi narrated to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan—narrated to us: Abu Yunus al-Qushayri narrated to us: Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "No one is brought to account except that he perishes." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, does not Allah say: 'an easy reckoning'?" He said: "That is the presentation of deeds; but whoever is called to a detailed reckoning will perish."
Abu ar-Rabi' al-'Ataki and Abu Kamil both narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us with this chain of narration, similar to it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Ali ibn Hujr both narrated to us, from Isma'il; Abu Bakr said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever is audited on the Day of Resurrection will be punished." I said, "Has not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {'He will surely receive an easy reckoning'}?" He said: "That is not the reckoning; that is only the presentation of deeds. Whoever is called to a detailed reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be punished."

Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Ma'ni narrated to me: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Talhah; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik mentioned to us from Abu Talhah, who said: On the day of Badr, when the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gained victory over them, he ordered that twenty-some men—and in the hadith of Rawh: twenty-four men—from the chieftains of Quraysh be thrown into one of the dried-up wells of Badr. And he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Thabit from Anas.

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, left the slain of Badr for three days, then came to them and stood over them and called out to them, saying: "O Abu Jahl ibn Hisham! O Umayyah ibn Khalaf! O 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah! O Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah! Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." 'Umar heard the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can they hear and how can they respond when they have decayed into corpses?" He said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you do not hear what I say any better than they do, but they are unable to respond." Then he ordered that they be dragged and cast into a well of Badr.
